claim: God withholds what we crave when it would harm us, as a doctor refuses a sick man harmful food.

heals.why: the wish that was refused may have been the one that would have hurt
Narada's craving is treated as a fever, not as a need

cultivates.why: a refusal can be an act of care

needs: trust that a caring Lord stands behind what is granted and refused

commentary.reading: Narada, proud of having conquered Kama, is seized by desire; the Lord, as a physician guarding his devotee from pride, refuses the boon for his good.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Help that comes after the moment has passed is useless, so act while it still matters.

heals.why: delay has a price that later regret cannot repay
the moment is named as something that ends

cultivates.why: the closing moment itself becomes the reason to move now

commentary.reading: Seeing Sita's anguish, Ram reflects that help after the hour is worthless and moves to lift the bow; the lines are quoted as niti on timely action.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Sharp replies feed another's anger like ghee on fire; cool words quiet it.

heals.why: anger in a room grows by what is fed to it

cultivates.why: Ram answers rage with water-like words and the fire goes down
the calm one in the room sets its temperature

commentary.reading: Lakshman's retorts are oblations into Parashurama's fire; Ram, seeing it rise, speaks cooling words. The doha shows Ram's sheel and skill in speech.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Anger is the root of wrongdoing; in its grip people act wrongly and turn against everyone.

heals.why: names what anger makes a person do and whom it turns them against

commentary.reading: A true maxim, but Lakshman says it laughing, as a taunt to an enraged sage; in the scene it inflames rather than cools.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Anger cannot mend what is already broken.

heals.why: anger does nothing to the loss it is about

commentary.reading: Lakshman's vyangya to Parashurama: mock politeness that stokes the sage further. True as a saying, but it is the ghee in this scene, not the water.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Discernment does not arise without good company, and such company comes easily only by Ram's grace.

heals.why: confusion is partly a matter of whose company one keeps

cultivates.why: clear judgement is grown among good people, not alone

commentary.reading: Satsang is the root of joy and blessing and the fruit of all sadhana; viveka is impossible without it, and it is had by Ram's kripa.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: Minor: the line drops the second half, that such company comes by Ram's grace. Acceptable for a general reader.

claim: Even the most detached sage breaks down when his daughter leaves home.

depicts.why: a father famed for calm loses his composure at the parting
he holds her to his heart knowing she is leaving

heals.why: if Janaka wept, tears are no failure of wisdom

commentary.reading: Janaka, called param viragi, loses dhirata on seeing Sita leave; the great boundary of his gyan is washed away by love. Tulsidas honours the love, he does not fault it.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Love makes two one as water sells for milk, but deceit separates them and the sweetness goes.

heals.why: names what broke the closeness: something hidden

cultivates.why: closeness lives on nothing being concealed

commentary.reading: Tulsidas comments on Sati concealing her test of Ram from Shiva: in true love water gets the price of milk, and the sourness of kapat splits them.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: One may visit kin uninvited, but going where someone holds hostility toward you brings no good.

heals.why: the hurt of being unwelcome is met with permission to stay away

cultivates.why: self-respect may decline a room that holds contempt
custom allows the visit, judgement looks at the host's heart

commentary.reading: Shiva to Sati before Daksha's yajna: to a friend, master, father or guru one may go unasked, yet where there is virodh no good comes. The arc bears him out: Sati is insulted there.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Creation mixes virtue and fault; the wise take the virtue and leave the fault.

heals.why: fault in people and things is the given mixture, not a betrayal

cultivates.why: the swan's skill of separating
choosing to see what is good in a person

commentary.reading: The Creator made the world of guna and dosha together; saints, like the hamsa, take the milk of virtue and leave the water of fault.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: True resolve does not break even if the body does, as gold keeps its nature in fire.

heals.why: others' mockery of a chosen path is answered without wavering

cultivates.why: a resolve that does not bargain when tested
she answers those who belittle her choice with composure

commentary.reading: Parvati to the Saptarishis who test her by running down Shiva and Narada: born of the mountain, her hath will not leave though the body may. Read as ananya nishtha.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: Minor: 'Hold to what you are' is added. Closer: 'Gold is born of stone, and even in fire it stays gold. My resolve will hold even if this body does not.'

claim: Most people rejoice only in their own gain; rare is the good person who rejoices at another's rise.

heals.why: not rising at another's rise is the common default, and there is a larger way to be

cultivates.why: the ocean swelling at another's full moon

commentary.reading: Tulsidas: most are like ponds and rivers that swell with their own water; the rare sajjan is like the sea, rising at the sight of the full moon.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Ram, told he alone will be crowned, feels it unjust to brothers who shared everything with him.

heals.why: the favoured one himself questions being raised above his siblings
honour arrives and his first thought is of those left out

cultivates.why: a joy that wants to be shared

commentary.reading: On hearing of his coronation Ram feels loving regret that the eldest alone is anointed; Tulsidas prays that this regret remove the crookedness of devotees' hearts.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: Out of scene the line sounds like a passed-over sibling's complaint. It is the chosen one's unease. Corrected: 'We grew up sharing every milestone. It troubled him that he alone was to be crowned.'

claim: Gain and loss, meeting and parting come by time and karma like day and night; the steady hold both alike.

heals.why: the loss is placed inside a rhythm no one escapes
what comes by time is not held off by worry

cultivates.why: holding joy and sorrow alike
patience taken up through discernment

needs: that the reader is past the first shock and can hear a wider view

commentary.reading: Sumantra tries to steady Dasharath with the teaching of kala and karma. The teaching is sound, but in the arc the king cannot take it in and dies of separation.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: What time and karma brought could not be turned; do not carry this loss as your own shame.

heals.why: the person with the most right to blame him says the shame is not his
a grieving mother asks him to hold on, so he is not alone in it

cultivates.why: courage asked for one day at a time, 'even now'

commentary.reading: Kausalya, herself bereaved, comforts Bharat: knowing the course of kala and karma to be unalterable, do not take loss and glani to heart.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: In grief, hold courage in the heart and do what this moment requires.

heals.why: grief is given one next task
he rises on hearing it

cultivates.why: courage held in the heart while the hands work

commentary.reading: Vasishtha asks the shattered Bharat to take heart and do the duty of the hour, his father's last rites; Bharat rises and arranges everything.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Advice can be sound and fully understood, and the heart can still find no rest in it.

depicts.why: every elder's sound advice points one way and his heart the other
understanding does not reach the grief

commentary.reading: Bharat respectfully grants that guru and mother advise what is good for him, yet says his heart finds no paritosh in it; his peace lies only in going to Ram.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Though I am the cause of this harm, if I go to him for refuge he will forgive.

depicts.why: he calls himself the guilty cause of everything

heals.why: guilt is carried toward the wronged person instead of away from him

cultivates.why: he trusts the other's heart more than his own record

needs: knowing that Bharat is in fact innocent and takes the blame out of love

commentary.reading: Bharat's dainya: he counts himself the root of the calamity yet trusts Ram's nature to forgive one who comes for sharan. The tradition holds Bharat blameless.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Acting in haste brings regret; learn a person's nature and intent before you fight them.

heals.why: suspicion is not yet knowledge of the other's heart

cultivates.why: he stops, listens to an elder and checks first

commentary.reading: Guha, ready to fight Bharat for Ram's sake, accepts the old man's counsel: fools act in haste and repent; first learn Bharat's sheel and intent.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Do not carry shame for your mother's deed; she too is not to blame, for her mind was clouded.

heals.why: a sage lifts a family member's act off the one who did not do it
the mother too is released, so he need not hate her

commentary.reading: Bharadwaj to Bharat: feel no glani over Kaikeyi's deed; even she is not at fault, since Saraswati deluded her mind for the gods' purpose.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: Fine as a line, but the second half (the parent is not to blame) holds only inside the story and must not be told to someone harmed by a parent.

claim: Think a deed through before doing it; those who act in haste and repent are not wise.

heals.why: protective anger is asked to look before it strikes

cultivates.why: weighing first, then acting

commentary.reading: The akashvani praises Lakshman's strength, then counsels that any deed, fit or unfit, be done after reflection; haste followed by regret is not wisdom.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Some counsel sounds sweet and ends in ruin, like poison mixed in honey.

heals.why: advice is to be judged by where it leads, not by how it sounds

cultivates.why: tasting for the poison under the honey

commentary.reading: Tulsidas on Manthara's speech to Kaikeyi: soft to hear, harsh in its end, like honey mixed with poison.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Ram goes first to the mother who exiled him and comforts her, laying the blame on time and fate.

heals.why: the one wronged moves first and holds nothing against her

cultivates.why: forgiveness given from strength to one already sunk in remorse
he sees her shame and eases it

needs: that the reader has chosen to forgive and is looking for how

commentary.reading: At Chitrakoot Ram meets Kaikeyi first, who is consumed by remorse, and consoles her by putting the blame on kala, karma and vidhi: the world is in God's hands, blame no one.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: A person in distress cannot speak with weighed judgement; like a gambler he sees only his own stake.

heals.why: distress narrows sight to one's own stake, so the decision can wait or be handed to someone steadier

cultivates.why: knowing when one's own judgement is not to be trusted

commentary.reading: Vasishtha includes himself among the distressed and so asks Ram to decide what is good for all. It is humility about one's own judgement, not a dismissal of those who suffer.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: Out of scene the line can read as dismissing people in pain. Closer: 'In distress none of us weighs things well. The gambler sees only his own throw.'

claim: Ram never once broke his younger brother's heart, and even let him win the games he lost.

cultivates.why: remembering one specific kindness of an elder
a picture of how the stronger one can treat the smaller

commentary.reading: Bharat before the assembly recalls Ram's affection from childhood: he never left Ram's company, and Ram never hurt his feelings, letting him win even lost games.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Your shame is baseless; a soul's course lies in God's hands, and you stand above all the virtuous.

heals.why: the very person he believes he wronged tells him the shame is for nothing
he is told plainly where he stands in his brother's eyes

needs: that the reader's guilt is larger than anything they actually did

commentary.reading: Ram to Bharat at Chitrakoot: you feel glani in vain, the jiva's course is under Ishvara; in my view the holy of all three times and worlds are beneath you.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: The dread was self-made and had no root; when one loses direction the sun is not to blame.

depicts.why: looking back, he sees he lived in a fear of his own making

heals.why: a rejection he was sure of turned out to have no ground
he stops blaming the one he feared

needs: that the feared thing is a guess about someone's heart, not a real threat

commentary.reading: Bharat, reassured by Ram and the guru, says he feared from apdar, his own false apprehension, and that the fault lay in his fortune and the times, never in Ram.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: As gold is known on the touchstone, a person is known by how they act when time tests them.

heals.why: the hard season is where one's quality gets to show

cultivates.why: being tested is treated as assay, not punishment
worth is proved by conduct, not by others' word

commentary.reading: Kausalya to Sunayana in praise of Bharat: gold is tested by rubbing, a gem by the jeweller, and a man by his nature in the hour of trial.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: In hard times it is good brothers who take the blow, as hands rise to shield against a thunderbolt.

cultivates.why: taking the hard share for one's family when times are bad
a gentle person is asked to carry something heavy

commentary.reading: Ram, knowing Bharat's tenderness, asks him the hard thing, to rule in his absence: in an evil hour good brothers are the help, as the hands ward off even the thunderbolt.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: A leader should be like the mouth: it alone eats, yet with discernment it nourishes every limb.

heals.why: position is redefined as the place through which everyone else is fed
what the leader takes in is not his to keep

cultivates.why: leading as nourishing

commentary.reading: Ram's parting counsel on rajadharma to Bharat: the chief should be like the mouth, which alone eats and drinks yet with viveka sustains all the limbs.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Ram receives his exile as good fortune, glad that his beloved brother gains the throne.

heals.why: a brother's gain is counted as his own

cultivates.why: the loss of a throne is met without a change of face
he counts what the forest gives him

needs: that the reader is not in fresh hurt over a loss

commentary.reading: Ram to Kaikeyi: sages' company in the forest, his father's command, her wish and Bharat's kingship all favour him; not to go for such a cause would be folly.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: A crooked mind takes even plain, sincere words as crooked.

heals.why: being misread is located in the reader's mind, not in what you said
you need not keep re-examining honest words

commentary.reading: Ram's words were sahaj, but Kaikeyi in her kumati took them as crooked, as a leech moves crookedly even in level water.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: To Ram the kingship was a tether; hearing of exile he felt freed and his joy grew.

heals.why: a role everyone envies can also be a chain

cultivates.why: losing the post, he feels unbound
joy rises where grief was expected

needs: that the reader is ready to see what the loss opened

commentary.reading: Ram's mind is a newly caught elephant and the kingdom its tying post; hearing of the forest he knows himself released and his heart's joy increases.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: A mother's true love does not hold her son back from his duty; she asks only to be remembered.

depicts.why: she lets him go and can ask only not to be forgotten
she has weighed keeping him against what is right

cultivates.why: love that releases instead of holding

commentary.reading: Kausalya, weighing dharma, decides not to press Ram with a show of affection that would make him fail his father's word; she only asks him to keep the tie of a mother.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: A mother parting from her child wonders whether she will live to see that face again.

depicts.why: the parting has begun and she is already counting the days
she fears she may not be alive at the return
she asks fate whether her fortune will ever turn

commentary.reading: Kausalya at the leave-taking: will my condition turn again, when will the blessed hour come that the mother, still living, sees your moon-like face.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Ayodhya is wherever Ram lives, as day is wherever the sun shines.

heals.why: home is placed in a presence, not in a town

cultivates.why: where the Lord is, there is one's place
she sends her son to serve

commentary.reading: Sumitra to Lakshman: Avadh is where Ram dwells; if Sita and Ram go to the forest you have no work here. For the devotee the Lord's presence is home.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: The line replaces Ram with 'your people', which secularises the verse. Corrected: 'Ayodhya is wherever Ram lives, as day is wherever the sun shines.'

claim: No one is the giver of another's joy or sorrow; each lives out the fruit of their own deeds.

heals.why: the authorship of one's pain is taken back from the person blamed
there is no outside giver to be angry at

cultivates.why: joy and sorrow both traced to one source

needs: acceptance of karma; the reader must be asking why, not asking to be heard

commentary.reading: The Lakshman Gita: Guha grieves at Ram on the ground and blames Kaikeyi; Lakshman answers with jnana and vairagya that each one tastes his own karma.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Knowing this, do not be angry or blame anyone; all are asleep in delusion's night, seeing dreams.

heals.why: the one who hurt you is seen as asleep, not as an enemy
blame loses its object

cultivates.why: seeing the world's play as dream

needs: willingness to take the Vedantic view of the world as dream-like

commentary.reading: Continuing the Lakshman Gita: therefore do not be angry or fault anyone in vain; all sleep in the night of moha and see many dreams.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: Minor: the line keeps the instruction and drops the reason. Fuller: 'Do not give way to anger or blame anyone needlessly. Everyone is asleep in the night of delusion, dreaming.'

claim: Having served Ram, the boatman counts himself paid in full and wants nothing more.

cultivates.why: one act of service is felt as complete wages
he counts what he has received instead of what he is owed

commentary.reading: Kevat refuses Sita's ring: what have I not gained today; long have I laboured for wages, and today vidhi has paid me richly. His wage is having washed Ram's feet.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Devotion includes seeing all the world as filled with Ram, being content with what comes, and seeing no one's faults.

heals.why: fault-finding is given up even in dreams
whatever comes is enough

cultivates.why: contentment named as a form of devotion
seeing the Lord in everyone

commentary.reading: The seventh and eighth of the nine forms of bhakti Ram teaches Shabari: seeing the world as Ram-filled and saints as greater than him; contentment with what is got and no fault-finding.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: Minor: the line reads as general advice; in the verse these are forms of devotion to Ram.

claim: Good people shrink from their own praise, delight in praise of others, and stay even, simple and loving to all.

heals.why: praise of oneself is met with discomfort, not appetite
another's praise is heard with delight

cultivates.why: affection toward everyone as one's nature

commentary.reading: Ram to Narada on the marks of saints: abashed at hearing their own virtues, glad at others', even and cool, never leaving niti, simple and loving to all.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: The body of five elements lies here and the soul is eternal, so there is no one to weep for.

heals.why: the one she loved was never only the body lying there

cultivates.why: the jiva is nitya
with understanding she asks for devotion

needs: grief already voiced and heard; this is week 3 material, never a first word

commentary.reading: Ram gives the distraught Tara jnana and removes her maya: the body is of five elements, the jiva eternal. The understanding comes by his grace, and she asks for bhakti.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: The learned grow humble with knowledge, and the good bear the wicked's harsh words as mountains bear rain.

heals.why: harsh words are pictured as rain on rock

cultivates.why: bearing words without being moved by them
the mountain does not answer each drop

commentary.reading: Ram's monsoon similes to Lakshman: clouds bend low as the wise bow on gaining vidya; hills endure the drops as saints endure the words of the wicked.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Good qualities gather in a good person little by little, as water collects to fill a pond.

heals.why: the river grows still on reaching the sea

cultivates.why: growth is slow gathering, not a leap
the soul rests on finding Hari

commentary.reading: Water gathers into the ponds as virtues come to the good man; the river's water becomes still in the ocean as the jiva does on attaining Hari.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Nothing intoxicates like sense pleasures; they delude even a sage's mind in a moment.

depicts.why: he admits that comfort made him forget what he owed

heals.why: the lapse is named as one even sages fall to, so it can be owned

commentary.reading: Sugriva, having forgotten Ram's work in the pleasures of kingship, confesses to Lakshman that there is no mada like vishaya. Humility is accepted and he is reassured.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: 'Comfort' is softer than vishaya, the pleasures of the senses. Closer: 'Nothing intoxicates like pleasure. It can cloud even a sage's mind in a moment.'

claim: Seeing Sampati's body restored by Ram's grace, take heart: the task can be done.

heals.why: living proof stands before them that ruin is not final

cultivates.why: a party that had sat down to die gets up
grace has visibly acted once already

commentary.reading: Sampati to the despairing monkeys: whoever leaps the hundred yojanas will do Ram's work; look at me and take courage, see what my body has become by Ram's kripa.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: The line omits the cause the verse gives. Corrected: 'Look at me and take heart. See what Ram's grace has done to this body.'

claim: No task in the world is too hard for you; you were born for Ram's work.

heals.why: an elder names the strength he had forgotten
the silent doubt is answered with his purpose

cultivates.why: on hearing it he grows to the size of a mountain

commentary.reading: Jambavant rouses the silent Hanuman: what work is hard for you, your very birth is for Ram's task. Strength returns when he is reminded of whose work it is.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: Minor: 'You were made for this' drops 'for Ram's work', which is the source of the strength in the verse.

claim: A true friend counts his own mountain of sorrow as dust and a friend's speck of sorrow as a mountain.

cultivates.why: friendship measured by whose trouble weighs more
being pained by a friend's pain

commentary.reading: Ram to Sugriva on mitra dharma: it is sin even to look at those not grieved by a friend's grief; one's own mountain of sorrow is dust beside a friend's speck.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: To one drowning in separation, a messenger from the beloved is a ship.

depicts.why: she calls her separation a sea she was going under in

cultivates.why: she names the one who reached her

commentary.reading: Sita, knowing Hanuman to be the Lord's servant, is overcome with love: I was sinking in the ocean of viraha and you have become my boat.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Speaking of sorrow lightens it, but this sorrow has no one who would understand it.

depicts.why: Ram himself has no one to tell
the ache is his alone to carry

commentary.reading: Ram's message to Sita: grief is lessened by telling, but to whom shall I tell it; the essence of our love only my mind knows, and that mind stays with you.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Hanuman matches the obstacle by growing, then passes it by becoming very small.

heals.why: the contest of size is won by giving it up

cultivates.why: knowing when to rise to a challenge and when to slip past it
he meets a test with play, not dread

commentary.reading: Surasa, sent by the gods to test Hanuman's strength and wit, widens her mouth; he doubles, then turns tiny, enters and leaves. She blesses him as fit for Ram's work.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: All the joys of heaven and liberation together do not equal one moment of good company.

heals.why: a single moment of true company is counted above every other good

cultivates.why: the joy of being with the good
even a blow from a saint is received as fortune

commentary.reading: Lankini, struck by Hanuman and recalling Brahma's sign, counts the touch of a saint her great merit: heaven and apavarga in one pan do not weigh a moment of satsang.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Hanuman credits his whole feat to Ram's power and none of it to himself.

heals.why: at the moment of highest praise he hands the credit away
success is not allowed to go to his head

cultivates.why: the strength was lent, so the glory is returned

needs: this is for someone carrying success, never for someone who doubts their worth

commentary.reading: Asked how he crossed the sea and burned Lanka, Hanuman says it was all Ram's pratap and no prabhutai of his own; the tradition holds this up as the mark of the true servant.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: When minister, physician and teacher say only what pleases, from fear or hope of gain, kingdom, body and dharma soon perish.

heals.why: pleasant words from those meant to tell the truth are named as a danger

cultivates.why: valuing the adviser who risks displeasing
the duty to say the unwelcome thing

commentary.reading: Tulsidas on Ravana's flattering ministers: if sachiv, vaidya and guru speak sweetly out of fear or hope, then rule, health and dharma are quickly lost.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: No power survives enmity toward living beings, and even a little greed ruins a gifted person's name.

heals.why: even a small greed is shown to undo every other merit
lordship of fourteen worlds does not protect one who harms others

commentary.reading: Vibhishan's counsel to Ravana in court: the sole lord of fourteen worlds cannot stand if he is hostile to beings; no one speaks well of a virtuous man with a little greed.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Good and bad judgement live in every heart; good judgement brings prosperity and bad judgement brings ruin.

heals.why: both voices are in everyone, so hearing the worse one is no special shame
outcomes are tied to which counsel one follows

cultivates.why: choosing sumati deliberately

commentary.reading: Vibhishan to Ravana: Puranas and Vedas say sumati and kumati dwell in every heart; where sumati is there is wealth of every kind, where kumati, disaster in the end.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Having warned his brother in vain and been struck, Vibhishan leaves for Ram's refuge and asks not to be blamed.

heals.why: he does not stay to be struck again
loyalty to family ends where the family has chosen ruin

cultivates.why: he leaves openly, having said the true thing

commentary.reading: Kicked by Ravana for honest counsel, Vibhishan declares that Ram's resolve is true and the court is in the grip of kala, and goes to Raghuvir's sharan. The tradition honours the leaving.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: 'I've said what I had to say' is not in the verse, and the refuge in Ram is dropped. Corrected: 'Your court is in the grip of its own ruin. I am going to Ram for refuge now. Do not blame me.'

claim: Even one with the power to force a matter should first make a humble request.

heals.why: strength is asked to begin with courtesy

cultivates.why: restraint chosen by the one who could compel
niti sets the order, request first

commentary.reading: Vibhishan advises Ram to petition the ocean though one arrow could dry it. Whole arc: three days of humble asking, then the bow. Humility first, but not without limit.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Pleading with the stubborn and good counsel to the unreceptive are wasted, like seed sown in barren ground.

heals.why: patience that was ignored is allowed to end
continuing to plead is no longer required of him

cultivates.why: after real humility, firmness is right
fitting the approach to the one in front of you

needs: the three days of humble asking that come before; firmness follows patience, it does not replace it

commentary.reading: After three days of vinaya the ocean does not yield and Ram calls for his bow, listing mismatched efforts as seed on barren land. The ocean then comes in submission and Ram spares it.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: The line keeps two minor items and drops the head of the verse. Corrected: 'Pleading with the stubborn and kindness to the crooked are seed sown in barren ground.'

claim: A good person among the hostile lives like the tongue among teeth, unsure if grace will ever reach him.

depicts.why: he is the only one of his kind in his own house
the tongue must move with care or be bitten
he calls himself without a protector and doubts he will be taken in

commentary.reading: Vibhishan to Hanuman: my living here is like the poor tongue among the teeth; will the Lord of the solar line ever show kindness to me, an anath.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Remembering a brother who waits at home, every moment away feels like an age.

depicts.why: comfort is offered and his mind is already at home with the one waiting

commentary.reading: Ram declines Vibhishan's hospitality after the war: your treasury and house are mine, but remembering Bharat's condition each nimisha passes like a kalpa.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Speak with an opponent so that your purpose is served and his good as well.

heals.why: the opponent's good is kept in the aim

cultivates.why: the envoy is trusted to find the words
goodwill held even toward the enemy

commentary.reading: Ram to Angad before the embassy: I know you are most able, what more to teach; speak with the enemy so that our work is done and his welfare too.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: A good person's mind does not abandon what is right though countless obstacles come.

cultivates.why: a foot that will not lift from the ground
holding to niti through a million hindrances
standing alone and unshaken in a hostile court

commentary.reading: Angad's planted foot cannot be moved by Ravana's warriors and the enemy's pride drains away; Tulsidas likens it to the saint's mind that never forsakes niti.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Ram, holding his fallen brother, recalls how Lakshman left everything and bore every hardship for him.

depicts.why: he speaks to one who cannot answer
the night is passing and help has not come
all that was suffered was suffered for his sake

commentary.reading: Ram's lament over Lakshman struck by the shakti, in the manner of a man: you could never see me sad; for me you left father and mother and bore cold, heat and wind.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Many are skilled at advising others; few practise what they advise.

heals.why: fine talk is separated from the life behind it

cultivates.why: measuring teaching by the teacher's conduct, starting with oneself

commentary.reading: Ravana preaches jnana to his grieving queens while himself in the wrong; Tulsidas remarks that experts in advising others are many, practitioners few.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: The chariot that wins is made of valour, patience, truth, conduct, self-control, forgiveness, compassion and evenness.

heals.why: the frightened friend is shown that the real equipment is already present
being outmatched in means is not being outmatched

cultivates.why: patience named as a wheel of victory
character as the banner one fights under

commentary.reading: The Dharma Rath: Vibhishan fears for Ram, who stands on foot against the charioted Ravana; Ram answers that the chariot of victory is built of virtues.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Ram credits his victory to his companions and calls them dearer to him than his own brother.

heals.why: the victor names those who carried him

cultivates.why: thanks given publicly and specifically
friends honoured above kin

commentary.reading: Ram presents the vanaras to Vasishtha: these friends were my ships across the sea of battle, they staked their lives for me, they are dearer to me than Bharat.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: A soul in maya's grip wanders astray without knowing it, so it deserves mercy and not anger.

heals.why: the offender is seen as lost, not as wicked

cultivates.why: the one insulted is the one who pleads for the offender
forgiveness asked on another's behalf

needs: that the reader is the stronger or elder party and has chosen to forgive

commentary.reading: The guru whom Kakbhushundi slighted begs Shiva to lift the curse: the jiva, deluded by your maya, ever strays; do not be angry with him, ocean of mercy.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: The line hides that the speaker is the wronged teacher praying to Shiva. Closer: 'He is lost in delusion and does not know it. Lord, do not be angry with him.'

claim: Through many births one pain never left him: the memory of the gentle teacher he had insulted.

depicts.why: remorse that outlasts lifetimes, and it is the other's kindness that hurts most

commentary.reading: Kakbhushundi to Garuda: in every body I kept up Ram bhajan, yet one shool I never forgot, my guru's tender and gentle nature.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Repeated slights anger even the wise, as hard rubbing brings fire out of cool sandalwood.

heals.why: losing one's temper after long provocation happens even to the wise
anger is traced to friction applied again and again

commentary.reading: Kakbhushundi, who kept contradicting the sage Lomash, owns that the fault was his: much disrespect raises anger even in a jnani's heart, as friction draws fire from chandan.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Non-harm is the highest duty, and no sin is as heavy as slandering others.

heals.why: running others down is named as the gravest harm one does

cultivates.why: the saint's rising gladdens everyone like sun and moon

commentary.reading: Kakbhushundi's answers to Garuda: ahimsa is the supreme dharma known to the Veda, and there is no sin weightier than par ninda.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Delusion is the root of all the mind's diseases; desire, greed and anger are its wind, phlegm and bile.

heals.why: the many pains are given one root
anger is named as bile that burns one's own chest

commentary.reading: The manas rog passage: moha is the root of all disease; kama is vata, lobha kapha, krodha pitta. The cure given later is devotion to Ram under the sadguru as physician.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Seeing that Kaikeyi is ashamed, Ram goes first to her house and puts her at ease.

heals.why: the one wronged holds nothing and moves first
the ashamed person is sought out, not left to hide

cultivates.why: forgiveness given to one already sunk in remorse

needs: that the reader has chosen to forgive and is looking for how

commentary.reading: Shiva tells Parvati: the Lord knew Kaikeyi was ashamed, so he went first to her palace, consoled her and gave her joy, and only then to his own.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: With one day left and no word, Bharat fears he has been forgotten for his own unworthiness.

depicts.why: the mind supplies the worst reason for the silence
fourteen years of waiting come down to one day
he assumes he was dropped because he is crooked

commentary.reading: One day of the avadhi remains, the prop of Bharat's life; boundless grief rises: why has the Lord not come, has he forgotten me, knowing me false.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: As Bharat was sinking in separation, Hanuman arrived like a boat.

depicts.why: his mind is going under in the sea of separation

heals.why: word arrives at the lowest point of the wait

cultivates.why: the long faithfulness is answered

commentary.reading: Bharat's mind is sinking in the ocean of Ram viraha when Hanuman, in a brahmin's form, arrives like a ship. Narrative of an event, not a promise that rescue always comes.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: The good do good even to those who harm them, as sandalwood leaves its fragrance on the axe that cuts it.

heals.why: one's own nature is kept regardless of what the other does

cultivates.why: giving fragrance to the blade
goodness that does not wait for good treatment

needs: that the reader is out of the axe's reach and is asking who they want to be

commentary.reading: Ram on sant and asant: the axe cuts the Malaya tree, which still perfumes it. The next doha completes it: sandal is raised to the gods' heads, the axe is heated and hammered.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Bharat counts the news of Ram's return beyond any gift and himself forever in the messenger's debt.

cultivates.why: he says plainly that he can never repay
every sorrow ends at the sight of the messenger

commentary.reading: Bharat to Hanuman: at the sight of you all my sorrows are gone; I have searched and find nothing in the world equal to this message; I can never be free of this debt.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: The good are not greedy for pleasure, grieve at others' sorrow, rejoice at others' joy, and hold no one an enemy.

heals.why: another's joy is felt as one's own

cultivates.why: being pained by another's pain
without pride, greed, rage, elation or fear

commentary.reading: Ram to Bharat on the marks of saints: free of craving for sense objects, mines of sheel, sorrowing in others' sorrow and glad in their gladness, even and enemy-less.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: The good never waver from self-control or speak harshly, hold praise and blame alike, and give their love to Ram's feet.

heals.why: harsh speech is simply absent from them

cultivates.why: praise and blame received alike
their attachment rests in the Lord's feet

commentary.reading: Ram concludes the marks of the saint: firm in shama, dama, niyama and niti, never harsh in speech, alike to ninda and stuti, devoted to my feet; such are dear to me as life.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: The line turns a description of saints into commands and drops their devotion. Closer: 'They never speak a harsh word, and praise and blame land on them the same way.'

claim: No duty equals doing good to others, and no baseness equals causing others pain.

heals.why: a purpose is given that needs no special station

cultivates.why: others' good as the highest dharma
others' pain as the thing never to cause

commentary.reading: Ram to his brothers: there is no dharma like par hit and no vileness like par peeda; this is the settled conclusion of all Puranas and Vedas.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Ram asks his people to stop him without fear if he says anything unjust.

heals.why: the fear of correcting someone above you is lifted by the king himself
the one in power asks to be checked

cultivates.why: speaking up without fear
the right to say 'this is unjust' belongs to everyone

commentary.reading: Ram to the assembled citizens: he who follows my instruction is my dearest servant; yet if I say anything contrary to niti, brothers, forget fear and restrain me.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: One with no enmity, quarrel, craving or fear finds every direction full of joy.

heals.why: hope and dread are dropped together
no grudge and no quarrel to maintain

cultivates.why: joy that does not depend on which way one turns
neither wanting nor fearing anything

commentary.reading: Ram describes the devotee dear to him: without vair or vigraha, hope or fear, for whom all quarters are full of joy; undertaking nothing for self, homeless in attachment, prideless, sinless, angerless.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Ram says even Vaikuntha is not as dear to him as Ayodhya, the city of his birth.

heals.why: longing for one's birthplace is shared by the Lord himself

cultivates.why: love for the soil and river one comes from

commentary.reading: From the Pushpak Ram shows the vanaras Ayodhya: all praise Vaikuntha, yet it is not as dear to me as Avadhpuri, my janmabhumi, north of which flows the Sarayu.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Doubt is not cleared in a passing talk; it ends only through long time in good company.

heals.why: doubt is given time and company instead of a quick answer

cultivates.why: trust grows by staying near those who have it

commentary.reading: Shiva to the doubting Garuda: you met me on the road, how shall I instruct you; doubts break only when one keeps satsang a long while. He sends him to Kakbhushundi.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Only one scorched by the sun knows the worth of shade; his confusion is what led him to his teacher.

heals.why: the confusion he was ashamed of is seen as the road to what he found
doubt is honoured for where it took him

cultivates.why: thanks even for the scorching

commentary.reading: Garuda to Kakbhushundi after his doubt is cured: only he who is tormented by heat knows the joy of shade; had I not fallen into deep moha, how would I have met you.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Delusion, desire, craving and anger have overcome everyone; no one in the world is exempt.

heals.why: what he is ashamed of has happened to every being
falling to these forces is the common lot, not a personal defect

commentary.reading: Kakbhushundi consoles the ashamed Garuda: whom has moha not blinded, whom has kama not made dance, whom has trishna not maddened, whose heart has krodha not burned.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Envy, grief, worry and illusion have touched everyone; no one in the world is exempt.

heals.why: the snake of worry has bitten everyone
being shaken by grief or stained by envy is no special failing

commentary.reading: Continuing: whom has matsar not stained, whom has the wind of shoka not shaken, whom has the she-serpent chinta not bitten, whom has maya not pervaded.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: Minor: 'You are not the only one' is implied by the rhetorical questions but is not in the verse.

claim: A person's own defect or motion makes him misjudge what he sees, as one on a moving boat thinks the shore moves.

heals.why: the error is traced to the eye, not the moon

cultivates.why: checking one's own position before judging

commentary.reading: Kakbhushundi: those who attribute delusion to Ram are themselves deluded, like the jaundiced eye that calls the moon yellow or the boat passenger who sees the world moving.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: The Lord removes his servant's pride as a mother has her child's boil lanced, ignoring the cries for the sake of the cure.

heals.why: a humbling is read as surgery on pride
being cut down to size may have been the cure

cultivates.why: the hand that hurt was a mother's

needs: belief in a loving Lord, and a pain that was a humbling of pride and not harm done by another person

commentary.reading: Kakbhushundi: pride is the root of samsara's pains, so the merciful Lord removes it from his servant, as a mother has the boil cut though the child weeps.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Without devotion every virtue and pleasure is tasteless, like many dishes without salt.

heals.why: the full life that still tastes flat is given a reason

cultivates.why: he asks for devotion over every power offered

needs: that the reader is open to devotion as the answer

commentary.reading: Kakbhushundi, offered siddhis, jnana and moksha by the child Ram, reflects that all virtues and joys without bhakti are like dishes without salt, and asks for bhakti alone.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Without knowing there is no trust, without trust no love, and without love devotion does not hold.

heals.why: lack of feeling is traced back to lack of knowing

cultivates.why: trust built by coming to know
knowing is the first step, so asking is right

commentary.reading: Kakbhushundi: without knowing the Lord's greatness there is no pratiti, without pratiti no priti, and without priti bhakti is not firm, like oiliness on water.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: Fine, but the verse is about devotion to Ram. Using it for marriage distance stretches it.

claim: No one finds rest without natural contentment, however he strains, as a boat cannot move without water.

heals.why: rest is shown to be impossible while wanting continues
the wearing out by a million efforts is named

cultivates.why: contentment as the water the boat needs

commentary.reading: Kakbhushundi: can anyone find vishram without sahaj santosh; can a boat move without water though one die straining with a crore of efforts.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Manu grieves in old age that his life has passed at home without detachment or devotion to Hari.

depicts.why: a full and well-run life, and the sense that the essential was missed
he grieves over the years already spent

commentary.reading: Manu, a righteous king, finds the fourth stage of life upon him with no vairagya from sense objects and grieves that his birth has gone without Hari bhakti; he leaves for tapas.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: 'Grieved for the years spent elsewhere' hides what he grieved. Corrected: 'Old age had come and the pull of pleasures had not faded. He grieved that his life had gone by without devotion to God.'

claim: One who does not know the giver's greatness hesitates to ask for much, like a poor man before the wishing tree.

depicts.why: he feels too small to ask for what he truly wants
he doubts the giver can mean it

commentary.reading: Manu before the Lord: as a pauper who has found the kalpataru shrinks from asking for great wealth, not knowing its power, so doubt arises in my heart.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: A fine appearance deceives even the clever; the peacock is beautiful and sweet-voiced, and it eats snakes.

heals.why: being taken in is not proof of stupidity
appearance and voice are separated from conduct

cultivates.why: judging by what someone does, not how they look or sound

commentary.reading: Tulsidas on King Pratapbhanu deceived by the false ascetic: seeing a good guise not only fools but clever men are misled; see the peacock, nectar-voiced and a snake-eater.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Kausalya asks the Lord to put away his cosmic form and be simply her child, the joy she counts highest.

cultivates.why: the joy of a small child's play is preferred to a vision of God's majesty

commentary.reading: At Ram's birth Kausalya, overwhelmed by the four-armed form, asks him to give it up and do shishu lila; the Lord becomes an infant and cries. Vatsalya bhava is preferred to aishvarya.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: A father cannot bring himself to send his young son into danger.

depicts.why: he measures his tender son against terrible demons
the child is dear as his own breath
the parting is refused before it is accepted

commentary.reading: Dasharath to Vishwamitra: all my sons are dear as life and Ram I cannot give. In the arc Vasishtha persuades him and he sends both boys with the sage.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: The brave show their valour in deeds and do not announce it; cowards facing an enemy talk of their own prowess.

heals.why: self-announcement is named as the sign of weakness

cultivates.why: letting the deed speak

commentary.reading: Lakshman's retort to Parashurama's boasting. A true saying, used in the scene as a taunt that provokes the sage further.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: The library tags this for imposter feelings; it calls those who speak of themselves cowards and should not be shown to someone who feels small.

claim: Good company reforms even the wicked, and the good keep their own nature even in bad company.

heals.why: the worst can be changed by the company they keep
a good nature is not lost by a bad setting

cultivates.why: trust in the power of good company
keeping one's own quality like the gem on the serpent's hood

commentary.reading: Tulsidas: the wicked are reformed by satsang as base metal by the paras stone; if by fate the good fall into bad company they follow their own virtue like the serpent's gem.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Knowing the fault is her own, Sati cannot speak, and her heart burns within like a potter's kiln.

depicts.why: the fault is her own and there is nothing she can say
she reads in his manner that he has left her in his heart
a burning that has no outlet

commentary.reading: Sati reads Shiva's withdrawal and, knowing her own offence of testing Ram and concealing it, can say nothing; her heart smoulders like a kiln.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Whatever faults others list, the heart wants only the one it has settled on.

heals.why: a list of faults from others does not reopen her decision

cultivates.why: a choice held without needing others to agree
she grants their argument and still stands by her own

commentary.reading: Parvati to the Saptarishis: let Mahadev be a house of faults and Vishnu of all virtues; whose mind delights in whom, with him alone is its concern. Read as ananya nishtha and faith in the guru's word.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Everyone likes their own work; rare is the person who delights in another's.

heals.why: partiality to one's own is the common default
others' coolness to your work says little about the work

cultivates.why: becoming the rare one who is glad at another's

commentary.reading: Tulsidas: to whom is his own verse not pleasing, be it rich or flat; but those excellent men who rejoice on hearing another's composition are few in the world.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Envy's distress comes from one's own self-interest and delusion, not from any fault in the one envied.

heals.why: the unease is traced to one's own stake, not the other's rise
the threat was made by self-interest

commentary.reading: Brihaspati checks Indra, who fears Bharat's love will bring Ram back and wants to plot: you are distraught through selfishness; the fault is not Bharat's but your moha.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Do not torment yourself with baseless reasoning; love and enmity cannot be hidden, and your love is plain.

heals.why: the circling arguments against himself are named as kutarka
his love is visible, so he need not fear being misread

commentary.reading: Ram swears with Shiva as witness that the earth stands by Bharat's keeping, and tells him not to reason falsely against himself: enmity and love are never concealed.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: 'People know which you carry' can sound like a warning. In the scene it reassures. Corrected: 'Do not torment yourself with needless doubts. Love cannot be hidden, and yours is plain to everyone.'

claim: Service is the hardest duty because it conflicts with self-interest, and neither hatred nor love can judge clearly.

depicts.why: he knows his own love makes him unfit to judge his own case

cultivates.why: naming one's bias before deciding

commentary.reading: Bharat to Janaka: scripture and the world know seva dharma is hard; the master's duty opposes self-interest; enmity is blind and love has no discernment. So he leaves the decision to others.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Bharat's speech was simple yet deep, gentle yet firm, few in words and vast in meaning.

cultivates.why: being gentle and firm in the same breath

commentary.reading: Janaka and his court praise Bharat's reply: easy and unfathomable, soft, lovely and firm, of endless meaning in very few syllables.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Bharat lives amid royal wealth untouched by it, as lovers of Ram give up luxury like something vomited.

heals.why: wealth is all around and has no hold

cultivates.why: living in the garden without drinking from it
love of Ram leaves no appetite for luxury

commentary.reading: Bharat dwells in Ayodhya without raga like a bee in a champak grove; fortunate lovers of Ram renounce Lakshmi's pleasures as vomit.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Hemmed in by duty on one side and love on the other, a mother can neither keep her son nor let him go.

depicts.why: either choice costs her something she cannot give up
she is being asked to release her child

commentary.reading: Kausalya's mind is besieged by dharma and sneha, like the snake with the muskrat it can neither swallow nor release: keeping her son breaks dharma and divides the brothers.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Never come under attachment, anger, envy, pride or delusion; put them aside and serve with mind, deed and word.

heals.why: named among what must not rule him even in a dream
envy is to be left behind before service

cultivates.why: service with mind, action and speech

commentary.reading: Sumitra's parting teaching to Lakshman: do not even in dream fall under raga, rosha, irsha, mada and moha; giving up every vikara, serve Sita and Ram in thought, deed and word.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: There is no duty equal to truth, and to abandon it brings disgrace in all three worlds.

heals.why: the pull to turn back is settled by keeping one's word

cultivates.why: he holds to the vow against a loving plea
his honour rests on truth

commentary.reading: Ram to Sumantra, who begs him to return: Agama, Nigama and Purana declare no dharma equal to satya; I have got that dharma easily, and to leave it would spread ill fame.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: 'Abandoning it costs more than anything it saves' is not in the verse. Corrected: 'There is no duty equal to truth. It has come within my reach, and I will not give it up.'

claim: For one whose heart is given to others' good, nothing in the world is out of reach.

heals.why: a life spent for another is declared complete

cultivates.why: the good of others as what rules the mind

commentary.reading: Ram to the dying Jatayu, who fought Ravana for Sita: to those in whose mind par hit dwells nothing is hard to obtain; leave the body and go to my abode, you who lack nothing.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: The ninth devotion is being guileless with all and trusting Ram at heart, without elation or dejection; it is open to anyone.

heals.why: man or woman or any creature qualifies by even one of the nine

cultivates.why: neither elated nor downcast
reliance on Ram kept in the heart

commentary.reading: Ram completes navadha bhakti for Shabari: simplicity and guilelessness with all, trust in me, neither harsha nor dainya; whoever has even one of the nine is dear to me.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: The line drops 'trust in me', which is the centre of the ninth devotion. Fuller: 'Be simple and without guile with everyone, keep your trust in Ram, and be neither carried away nor cast down.'

claim: Desire, anger and greed are so strong that they unsettle even sages' minds in an instant.

heals.why: even sages are shaken, so being shaken is no disgrace
the three forces are named so they can be watched

commentary.reading: Ram to Lakshman at Pampa: kama, krodha and lobha are three most powerful villains that agitate in a moment the minds of munis who are abodes of wisdom.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Contentment dries up greed, and a heart freed of pride and delusion is clear like autumn water.

heals.why: greed is dried by contentment, not by getting more

cultivates.why: the rising star that dries the roads
a clear heart once pride and confusion have settled

commentary.reading: Ram's autumn similes: Agastya rises and dries the water of the paths as santosha dries lobha; rivers and lakes are clear like a saint's heart free of mada and moha.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: As ponds shrink the fish grow distressed, like an imprudent householder when the money runs out.

cultivates.why: providing for the dry season while the water is high

commentary.reading: Autumn simile: the fish are troubled as the water lessens, like an unwise householder without wealth. The word abudh, unwise, carries a judgement.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: Must not be shown to someone in money trouble: the verse calls the householder unwise. Use only for planning ahead.

claim: Sampati, in his pride, flew on toward the sun when his brother turned back, and fell with burned wings.

depicts.why: he names his own pride as the cause
the fall and the terrible cry

commentary.reading: Sampati tells the vanaras: Jatayu could not bear the heat and returned; I, abhimani, went near the sun, my wings burned and I fell crying to the earth. The Manas makes pride the cause.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Sugriva, in a moment of dispassion, calls his enemy brother his benefactor, since through him he met Ram.

heals.why: for a moment the feud looks like a dream

cultivates.why: the quarrel loses its grip in Ram's presence

commentary.reading: Sugriva says he would now be ashamed to fight Bali even in a dream. Ram smiles and says his own word will not prove false. The tradition reads this as kshanik vairagya: the feud continues.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: The line reads as a settled change of heart. In the story it is a passing mood, and the conflict with Bali goes on. Gate it or drop it; do not use it to counsel reconciliation.

claim: A friend turns you from the wrong path to the right, makes your virtues known and covers your faults.

cultivates.why: friendship defined by what it does for the other's good

commentary.reading: Ram on the friend: he keeps you from the evil path and leads you on the good, displays your virtues and conceals your faults; those without this feeling should not press friendship.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: A true friend gives and takes without suspicion, helps as far as he can, and loves a hundredfold more in hard times.

heals.why: tells the lonely what to look for and what to be

cultivates.why: love that multiplies in the friend's bad time
giving and taking without misgiving

commentary.reading: Ram: he has no doubt in giving and taking, always does good according to his strength, and in time of calamity loves a hundred times more; the Veda calls these a good friend's marks.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: One who speaks sweetly to your face and works harm behind your back is a false friend best given up.

heals.why: the two-faced friend is named, and leaving is called the good course

cultivates.why: reading the mind behind soft words
letting go of one who harms you

commentary.reading: Ram: he who speaks soft contrived words in front and is crooked and ill-wishing behind, whose mind moves like a snake, such a kumitra is better abandoned.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Wealth and power of one turned away from Ram are as good as lost, like rivers with no spring that dry after rain.

heals.why: power is shown to have no source of its own

cultivates.why: the spring that keeps the river is turning toward Ram

commentary.reading: Hanuman to Ravana: the wealth and lordship of one averse to Ram go even while they stay, got and yet not got, like rivers without a watered source.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: 'No deep source' hides what the verse names: being turned away from Ram. Closer: 'Wealth and power turned away from God are rain-fed rivers. They dry up when the rains stop.'

claim: The good do good even to those who harm them; struck by his brother, Vibhishan still tells him where his good lies.

heals.why: he is kicked and carries no hatred out with him

cultivates.why: goodwill toward the one who struck him
he repeats the true counsel even after the blow

needs: the next doha, where he leaves; goodwill here does not mean staying

commentary.reading: Shiva remarks that the saint's greatness is doing good to one who does him ill; Vibhishan, kicked, says you are as my father, yet your good lies in worshipping Ram. He then leaves Lanka.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: Shown alone, the line asks a mistreated person to keep wishing well. Use only with rcm.5.39.doha.1, where Vibhishan walks out.

claim: Whoever enters hard work holding Ram in the heart finds poison turn to nectar and enemies to friends.

heals.why: the hostile city is entered with the Lord held within

cultivates.why: ocean becomes a hoofprint and fire turns cool
the work is done with Ram kept in the heart

commentary.reading: Lankini blesses Hanuman: enter the city and do all your work keeping Kosala's king in your heart; for him on whom Ram looks with grace, poison is nectar and foes are friends.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: 'What you love' replaces Ram. Corrected: 'Enter the city and do all your work with Ram held in your heart. Then poison turns to nectar and enemies to friends.'

claim: A person of clean mind reaches Ram, who dislikes deceit, and Ram fears no loss in sheltering even a suspect.

heals.why: suspicion of a newcomer is answered from strength

cultivates.why: nothing to fear and nothing to lose from giving shelter
a clean mind is what is asked, nothing more

commentary.reading: Ram overrules Sugriva's suspicion of Vibhishan: the man of pure mind attains me, I do not like kapat and chhal; even if Ravana sent him to spy, there is no fear or harm.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: The line invents a general maxim about being trusted. Corrected: 'A person with a clean mind reaches me. I have no liking for deceit. And if he was sent to spy, we still have nothing to fear.'

claim: Living in hell is better than being forced into the company of the wicked.

depicts.why: years among people who despised what he held dear
he ranks his old life below hell

cultivates.why: he is well now, having been taken in

commentary.reading: Vibhishan to Ram: better to dwell in hell, may the Creator never give the company of the wicked; now, having seen your feet, I am well, since you have shown mercy knowing me your own.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Sound advice does not take on one bent on ruin, as medicine fails a person in death's grip.

heals.why: counsel that was thrown back failed because of the hearer, not the giver
he did say it, and need not keep trying

cultivates.why: knowing when advice can no longer land

commentary.reading: Prahasta, insulted by Ravana for honest counsel, says good advice suits him as medicine suits one under kala's sway, and leaves. Ravana goes off admiring his arms.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Kumbhakarna, though fighting for Ravana, praises Vibhishan for leaving him and calls him the ornament of their clan.

heals.why: the one who left the family for what is right is blessed by an elder brother
leaving is named as honour, not betrayal

cultivates.why: his choice is called the clan's pride

commentary.reading: Kumbhakarna to Vibhishan on the battlefield: Ravana is in death's power and will not heed counsel; thrice blessed are you, who have become the jewel of the nishachara line.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Take up enmity only with one you can overcome by wit and strength; Ravana beside Ram is a firefly beside the sun.

heals.why: his sense of his own size is corrected

cultivates.why: measuring the opponent before choosing a fight

commentary.reading: Mandodari pleads with Ravana: make enemies of one you can defeat by buddhi and bala; between you and Raghupati the gap is that of a glow-worm and the sun.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: As a general maxim it could tell a wronged person not to stand up to someone powerful. In the verse it is a wife warning an aggressor. Keep it inside the scene.

claim: Those devoted to Ram's feet, free of desire, pride and anger, see the world as filled with their Lord and oppose no one.

heals.why: no one is left to be an enemy
he takes a curse without bitterness

cultivates.why: seeing one's Lord in every being

commentary.reading: Shiva to Uma as Kakbhushundi accepts Lomash's curse calmly: those who love Ram's feet and are rid of kama, mada and krodha see the world as their Lord; with whom would they quarrel.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: Minor: 'the divine in everyone' drops that this vision belongs to those devoted to Ram's feet.

claim: Possessiveness, envy, the swings of elation and dejection, and burning at another's happiness are diseases of the mind.

heals.why: burning at another's joy is named as an illness one suffers, which can be treated

commentary.reading: The manas rog list continues: mamata is ringworm, irsha the itch, harsha and vishada throat disease, burning at another's happiness is consumption, wickedness and crookedness leprosy.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: To have a human body and not worship Hari is to throw away the philosopher's stone and take glass shards.

heals.why: the drift into pleasures is priced against what was given up

cultivates.why: the human birth is for worship of Hari

commentary.reading: Kakbhushundi: men who get this body and do not worship Hari, lost in base pleasures, drop the paras mani from their hand and take bits of glass.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: The line hides the verse's subject, which is not worshipping Hari. Using it for phone habits changes its proposition.

claim: There is no sorrow like poverty and no joy like meeting the good, whose nature is to help others.

heals.why: the pain of want is ranked as the world's greatest sorrow, not as a weakness

cultivates.why: the company of good people as the greatest joy
helping in word, thought and body

commentary.reading: Kakbhushundi answers Garuda: no dukh in the world equals daridrya, no sukh equals sant milan; doing good to others in word, mind and body is the saint's nature.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Angad, fatherless, begs Ram not to send him away: you are my lord, teacher, father and mother.

depicts.why: he has no one to go back to
he fears being sent away by the one he has left
he calls himself shelterless

cultivates.why: he asks to stay at Ram's feet

commentary.reading: Angad, whose father Bali is dead, at the farewell: remembering your vow as refuge of the refugeless, do not abandon me; where shall I go leaving your lotus feet.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Ram calls the boatman chief his friend and a brother equal to Bharat, and asks him to keep visiting.

heals.why: a man of low station is named brother by the king
the parting comes with an open door

cultivates.why: friendship kept across rank and distance

commentary.reading: Ram to Nishad Guha at parting: you are my friend, a brother like Bharat; keep coming to the city always. Guha falls at his feet with tears of joy.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: The wicked burn at the sight of another's prosperity and rejoice on hearing others slandered.

heals.why: envy is shown as a fire in the envier's own heart
the one who gloated at your fall is described exactly

commentary.reading: Ram on the asant: their hearts have a special heat, they burn seeing others' wealth, and where they hear another slandered they rejoice as if they had found treasure on the road.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: The path of devotion needs no yoga, sacrifice or fasting, only a simple nature, a mind without crookedness and contentment.

heals.why: no heroic practice is demanded
the path is open to someone with no attainments

cultivates.why: content always with what comes

commentary.reading: Ram to the citizens: what labour is there in the path of bhakti; it needs neither yoga nor yajna, japa, tapa or fasting, only a straight nature and constant contentment.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Ram never lets pride stay in his devotee, because pride is the root of rebirth and the giver of every sorrow.

heals.why: pride is named as the root of the pains that follow it

cultivates.why: the removal of pride is the Lord's care

commentary.reading: Kakbhushundi: it is Ram's nature never to leave abhiman in his servant, for abhiman is the root of samsara, giving many pains and all grief.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: A father loves all his differently gifted sons alike, yet the one devoted to him in thought, word and deed is dearest.

heals.why: different gifts do not mean different shares of love
a child need not be the scholar or the rich one to be loved

cultivates.why: devotion is what draws the Lord closest

commentary.reading: Ram to Kakbhushundi: a father's love is equal for all his sons, but the son devoted to him alone is dear as life; so all beings are mine, and the devotee is dearest.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: The line stops before the verse's point: the devoted son is dearest. Fuller: 'One father, many children, each different, and he loves them all alike. Yet the one wholly devoted to him is dearest.'

claim: In a degraded age teachers take money without removing sorrow, and parents teach children only what fills the belly.

cultivates.why: asking what one is really passing on to a child

commentary.reading: From the description of Kali Yuga: the guru who robs the disciple's wealth and not his sorrow falls into hell; mothers and fathers teach children the dharma of filling the stomach.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Though Ram is impartial, he has made action the law of the world: as one acts, so one tastes the fruit.

heals.why: what one does counts, by the world's own law

cultivates.why: act well, since action is what governs

commentary.reading: Brihaspati to Indra: the Lord is even, without raga or rosha, yet he has made the world karma-pradhan; whoever does as he does tastes such fruit. A warning against plotting.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: A petty person swaggers on a little wealth as small streams burst their banks after rain.

heals.why: swelling up over a small gain is pictured as a shallow stream

commentary.reading: Ram's monsoon similes: small rivers fill and break their banks as the base man is puffed up by a little wealth; water turns muddy on the ground as the jiva is wrapped by maya.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: What is destined is powerful: loss and gain, life and death, honour and dishonour lie in the Creator's hands.

heals.why: what happened was not his to prevent
the teacher weeps with him while he says it

cultivates.why: footing found in what was never in one's control

needs: said to lift guilt after a loss, never to explain away a wrong done by someone

commentary.reading: Vasishtha, himself in tears, to Bharat: bhavi is strong; hani, labh, jivan, maran, jas and apjas are in vidhi's hands. Spoken to free a blameless son of guilt.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: 'Much of it' softens the verse, which says these lie in the Creator's hands. Closer: 'Loss and gain, life and death, praise and blame: these rest in the Creator's hands.'

claim: When three days of humble request are ignored, Ram speaks in anger: without fear there is no regard.

heals.why: being ignored after real humility is answered with firmness
he stops asking

cultivates.why: courtesy has a limit and he shows it

needs: the three days of asking before and the forgiveness after; never about love between people close to each other

commentary.reading: The ocean, jad, does not heed vinaya for three days; Ram then shows anger as niti requires. The ocean appears, begs pardon, and Ram spares it and takes its counsel.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

line_issue: Note for the library: the misuse note on rcm.5.56.chaupai.1 says this doha is deliberately not used, yet it is here as core. Decide one way. If kept, never serve it outside the ocean passage.

claim: Ram never turns away one who comes for refuge, whatever his sins; the moment a soul faces him, its past wrongs are destroyed.

heals.why: no record is too heavy to be received
the only condition is turning to face him

cultivates.why: coming for shelter as one is

needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

commentary.reading: Ram to Sugriva on receiving Vibhishan: even one guilty of slaying a crore of brahmins I do not abandon if he comes for sharan; when the jiva turns toward me the sins of a crore births perish.
commentary.source: Gita Press tika (Hanuman Prasad Poddar), plain sense

claim: Ram will keep as dear as his own life anyone who comes to him afraid and seeking refuge.

heals.why: the frightened one is promised safekeeping
he will be held as dear as life

cultivates.why: shelter that does not ask where one came from
coming in fear is enough
